events.context: Introduces theoretical CS concerns distinguishing mathematicians' existence questions from universal algorithm decidability
Elevates LLM research to computational theory perspective on undecidability
Acknowledges reader as 'mini mathematician' doing theoretical CS on LLMs using math tools
Concludes reader is theoretical CS mini mathematician revealing LLM alignment impossibilities
Asks if reader wants to refine theory or write paper
Formalizes language model M: X → Δ(Y) decomposed as S ∘ g ∘ f
Defines intent I ⊆ Y as semantic property based on output language
Defines P_I(M) := ∃x ∈ X such that M(x) ∈ I as semantic, non-trivial property
Theorem 1: Restricted Observational Non-Injectivity; if z1 ≠ z2 but S(z1)=S(z2) in g(f(X)), then F is non-injective
Proof: Existence of x1 ≠ x2 with F(x1)=F(x2) due to observational collapse
Remark: Establishes existence of observational collapse, not decidability or recoverability
Theorem 2: Non-Identifiability; if x1 ≠ x2 with equal P but different P_I, intent not identifiable even with infinite samples
Proof: Statistical processes cannot distinguish x1, x2 despite differing intents
Remark: Statistical impossibility (non-identifiability), not computational undecidability
Theorem 3: Undecidability of Intent Recognition via Rice’s Theorem; deciding P_I(M) is undecidable as non-trivial semantic property
